source.title: Decoder-Preserving Sparse Autoencoders: Which Readouts Survive Sparse Compression?

record.tranche_reason: The study tests whether gains in readout preservation carry over to sparse-feature concept probes, and finds that they do not in one matched Pythia pair. It refines the scope of claims about SAE feature concentration, but does not test superposition geometry.
record.gate_note: The study's main decoder-distortion, reconstruction, and frozen-network results do not test the listed superposition claims and are omitted. The relevant results are the Pythia concept probes restricted to selected SAE features; these test concept recoverability/concentration, not feature overlap geometry or whether ordinary SAEs recover real-world features in an absolute sense.
record.test_reason: The study proposes decoder-preserving SAEs (DPSAE) and compares them with MSE-trained SAEs on readout distortion, frozen-model KL, IOI and concept probes. The Pythia concept-probe result compares the study's own SAE objective against a baseline SAE. It does not measure whether LLM features are spread across neurons, or whether sparse features exist or are recoverable in absolute terms. It also does not test toy-model geometry, polysemanticity causes, SAE feature canonicity, or feature dimensionality. SAEs serve as a tool, and the reported results concern the method's own performance.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that refitted readout fidelity, frozen-network compatibility, and sparse concept recovery are separate properties. DPSAE improves readout preservation at matched NMSE in GPT-2 but worsens IOI. In one matched Pythia pair it does not improve concentration of benchmark concepts into a few SAE features.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains decoder-preserving SAEs and evaluates concept probes; it does not reproduce the Toy Models of Superposition method.
record.method_sensitivity: The concept-probe result is conditional on one Pythia checkpoint pair and on the selected-feature budget k; the study reports results for k = 1, 2, and 5.

fits_no_version.finding: SAEs with equal MSE and L0 can preserve different linear readouts (Proposition 1). In GPT-2 block 8, a DPSAE matched in NMSE cuts held-out readout distortion by 10.6–11.4% yet lowers IOI accuracy by 0.88–2.39 pp. In Pythia, it does not improve sparse concept probes.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE reconstruction and sparsity do not uniquely determine which information the dictionary preserves. SAE solutions are underdetermined by their training loss, which bears loosely on whether dictionary features are canonical, though no feature-level stability is measured.

record.problems: The concept-concentration result uses one matched Pythia checkpoint pair, so it is conditional rather than evidence about a population of models. The study reports the primary k = 5 comparison numerically; k = 1 and k = 2 are described in text and shown in a figure without text-stated values.
record.rows_left_out: No additional claim-relevant results were reported. Full-code and full-reconstruction probe comparisons were described as near zero, but they do not measure recovery from a sparse set of selected features.

untested.parts: All: no toy-model superposition geometry, sparsity transition or feature overlap measured. The synthetic generator is overcomplete and nonorthogonal by construction, not a test of superposition.
All: no measure of neuron polysemanticity or capacity competition.
All: no measure of feature spread across neurons and no absolute test of SAE feature recovery; only DPSAE vs MSE comparisons.
All: completeness, stability and canonicity of SAE features are not measured.

record.verdict_notes: The reader labelled this a T5 test of V4, but the only linked results compare the study's own SAE objective with a baseline SAE. These are method-performance results (T4) and say nothing about whether LLMs exhibit superposition or contain SAE-recoverable sparse features. Verdicts are therefore removed. Row r1's state is changed to reversed because the DPSAE-minus-MSE difference is small but its interval excludes zero.

versions.untested_parts: Whether sparse features outnumber dimensions, overlap in nearly orthogonal directions, or show a sparsity-dependent geometric transition.
Whether neuron polysemanticity results from capacity competition, or whether important features receive dedicated dimensions.
Whether polysemanticity arises through mechanisms other than capacity pressure.

The study tests benchmark-concept probe performance on selected SAE features in one Pythia checkpoint pair; it does not test feature spreading across neurons or establish whether ordinary SAEs recover sparse features in an absolute sense or across models.
Whether SAE features are complete, stable, or canonical units of model representation.
Whether superposed features are one-dimensional directions rather than multidimensional features.

rows.subject: Pythia-160M-deduped
rows.operation_detail: L1 sparse probes restricted to selected SAE features; compare DPSAE with MSE reconstruction

conditions.value: 113 frozen labeled tasks grouped into 60 concept families

rows.measure: Family-macro test-AUROC difference, DPSAE minus MSE
rows.uncertainty: 95% family-block interval [−0.006910, −0.001150]; all ten probe-seed macro differences were negative, from −0.006643 to −0.000893
rows.note: The study says the matched pair does not improve concentration into five benchmark features. This is a relative difference, not an absolute test of whether SAE features recover concepts.
rows.check: Compares the study's own method (DPSAE) with an MSE SAE, so it is not evidence on V4. V4 concerns whether LLMs contain sparse features an SAE can recover, not which SAE objective concentrates concepts better. As a method comparison the gain is slightly reversed: −0.00387, CI excluding zero.

reader_labels.condition: One matched Pythia-160M-deduped block-8 pair; benchmark concept probes restricted to k = 1, 2, or 5 selected features
reader_labels.reason: Readout improvement did not translate into improved sparse-feature concept probe performance in this checkpoint pair (r1–r3); the result is conditional on one pair and does not resolve broader claims about SAE recoverability.
